title_en: Li Zhifang v. Traffic Management Authority — dispute over decision on re-determination of traffic accident liability

full_text_en:
Li Zhifang v. Traffic Police Detachment of Longyan Public Security Bureau, Fujian Province — dispute over traffic accident liability re-determination decision

Plaintiff: Li Zhifang, male, 30 years old, driver of Liancheng County Tobacco Company of Fujian Province, residing in Lianfeng Town, Liancheng County.

Agent ad litem: Wu Shengfa, legal worker of Liancheng County Legal Service Center of Fujian Province.

Defendant: Traffic Police Detachment of Longyan Public Security Bureau, Fujian Province.

Legal Representative: Ye Jianjin, Head of the Detachment.

Agents ad litem: Ye Qi and Chen Haiyan, officers of the Traffic Police Detachment of Longyan Public Security Bureau.

Third Party: Qiu Jialiu, male, 51 years old, worker, residing in Lianfeng Town, Liancheng County.

Third Party: Liu Lianhua, female, 42 years old, resident, wife of Qiu Jialiu, residing at the same address as above.

Third Party: Qiu Bingqin, male, 41 years old, farmer, residing in Jiele Township, Liancheng County.

Third Party: Xie Xiaoling, female, 40 years old, farmer, wife of Qiu Bingqin, residing at the same address as above.

Third Party: Zhou Lihua, female, 19 years old, resident, residing in Lianfeng Town, Liancheng County.

Third Party: Li Xia, female, adult, resident, residing in the dormitory of the Comprehensive Factory of Liancheng County Commercial Bureau.

On October 12, 2000, the defendant, Traffic Police Detachment of Longyan Public Security Bureau, Fujian Province (hereinafter referred to as Longyan Traffic Police Detachment), issued Document No. (2000) 343, "Decision on Re-determination of Road Traffic Accident Liability," determining: (1) Qiu Senbin, driving without a license, carrying passengers in violation of regulations which impeded driving, and occupying the oncoming lane, was one of the causes of the traffic accident; his conduct violated Article 6, Article 25, Article 33(1), and Article 49(1) of the Regulations on Road Traffic Management; (2) Li Zhifang, driving and occupying the oncoming lane, failing to comply with the principle of keeping to the right, was one of the causes of the traffic accident; his conduct violated Article 6 and Article 49(1) of the Regulations on Road Traffic Management. The Decision revoked the liability determination in Document No. 20001033, "Determination of Road Traffic Accident Liability," issued by the Traffic Police Detachment of Liancheng County, Fujian Province (hereinafter referred to as Liancheng Traffic Police Detachment), and re-determined that Qiu Senbin and Li Zhifang bear equal liability for the accident. The plaintiff, Li Zhifang, dissatisfied with this decision, filed an administrative lawsuit with the Liancheng County People's Court of Fujian Province.

Plaintiff's Allegations: The defendant's re-determination decision, which overturned the liability determination of Liancheng Traffic Police Detachment on the ground that the plaintiff occupied the oncoming lane, is erroneous. The determination that the plaintiff occupied the oncoming lane has no factual basis. We request that the defendant's re-determination decision be revoked in accordance with the law, and that the defendant be ordered to make a new liability determination.

Defendant's Defense: There are two causes of this major traffic accident. The liability of the plaintiff, Li Zhifang, is as follows: First, according to the "On-site Investigation Diagram of the Road Traffic Accident" and on-site photographs, the braking skid marks left on the road by Li Zhifang's emergency braking show a diagonal slide from 0.5 meters on the left side of the road's centerline to the right side, proving that Li Zhifang was driving on the opposite lane before detecting the danger. Because Li Zhifang failed to comply with the principle of keeping to the right and occupied the oncoming lane, Qiu Senbin misjudged Li Zhifang's driving dynamics during the meeting, leading to the accident. Second, the on-site investigation diagram shows that the accident section of the road is wide and straight with good visibility, allowing an early detection of the oncoming vehicle's movement. Based on Li Zhifang's braking pressure mark of 3.6 meters and skid mark of 15.1 meters, it can be determined that when Li Zhifang detected the danger, the distance from the oncoming vehicle should have been more than 30 meters. Within this distance, if the driver had responded in time and taken effective measures, the accident could have been avoided. However, due to Li Zhifang's excessive speed and negligence while driving, he took improper emergency evasive measures after detecting the danger. Of course, the other party, Qiu Senbin, driving a motorcycle without a license, carrying three passengers behind him which impeded maneuvering, and occupying the oncoming lane during the meeting, also contributed to the cause of the traffic accident. In summary, the defendant's liability determination is based on clear facts, reliable evidence, correct application of law, and lawful procedures. The People's Court should uphold the defendant's re-determination decision.

The defendant, Longyan Traffic Police Detachment, submitted to the court the testimonies of witnesses Lin Qincai and Wu Qiang, an on-site investigation sketch, a set of road traffic accident photographs, a technical appraisal report on the road traffic accident vehicles, and the interrogation record of Li Zhifang, among other evidence.

Facts Found by Liancheng County People's Court of Fujian Province:

On July 26, 2000, Qiu Senbin, son of the third parties Qiu Jialiu and Liu Lianhua, driving a two-wheel motorcycle (license plate Min FH2042) without a license, carrying three passengers: Qiu Lijun (daughter of third parties Qiu Bingqin and Xie Xiaoling), Zhou Lihua, and Li Xia, traveling from Wenheng direction towards Liancheng urban area. The plaintiff, Li Zhifang, driving a Jinbei brand minibus (license plate Min F60590), traveling from Liancheng urban area towards Wenheng direction. The two vehicles collided when meeting at the location of 175km+920m on the Jianwen Line, resulting in a major traffic accident: Qiu Senbin was injured and died after rescue efforts failed; Qiu Lijun died at the scene; Li Xia and Zhou Lihua were injured; both vehicles were damaged. On August 25 of the same year, Liancheng Traffic Police Detachment issued Document No. 20001033, "Determination of Road Traffic Accident Liability," determining: Qiu Senbin, driving without a license, carrying three passengers in excess of the limit, and occupying the oncoming lane, should bear primary responsibility for the accident; Li Zhifang, driving at excessive speed, being negligent, and taking improper measures in an emergency, should bear secondary responsibility. The third party, Qiu Jialiu, dissatisfied with the liability determination of Liancheng Traffic Police Detachment, applied for reconsideration to the defendant, Longyan Traffic Police Detachment. On October 12 of the same year, Longyan Traffic Police Detachment issued Document No. (2000) 343, "Decision on Re-determination of Road Traffic Accident Liability," revoking Document No. 20001033, "Determination of Road Traffic Accident Liability," made by Liancheng Traffic Police Detachment. It re-determined that Qiu Senbin, driving without a license, carrying passengers in violation of regulations which impeded driving, and occupying the oncoming lane, was one of the causes of the traffic accident and should bear equal liability for this accident; Li Zhifang, driving and occupying the oncoming lane, was one of the causes of the accident and should bear equal liability for this accident. Li Zhifang, dissatisfied with this re-determination, filed this lawsuit.

The above facts are confirmed by the evidence submitted by the defendant, Longyan Traffic Police Detachment, and the statements of the three parties. All evidence, after being examined and challenged during the court trial, can be used as the basis for determining the facts of this case.

Opinion of Liancheng County People's Court of Fujian Province:

The on-site investigation sketch and the road traffic accident photographs show that the tire braking skid marks of the Jinbei brand minibus driven by the plaintiff, Li Zhifang, began 0.5 meters to the left of the road centerline in the direction from Liancheng urban area to Wenheng, then diagonally entered the vehicle's own lane, and after moving forward approximately 6.15 meters, at a point 0.46 meters from the road centerline, appeared a turning point in the tire braking skid marks (i.e., the collision point of the two vehicles). This evidence proves that at the time of the collision, the Jinbei brand minibus driven by Li Zhifang was in its own lane, while the two-wheel motorcycle driven by Qiu Senbin was in the position of occupying the oncoming lane. The determination by the defendant, Longyan Traffic Police Detachment, that Li Zhifang's Jinbei brand minibus occupied the oncoming lane lacks factual basis and is erroneous; the determination that Qiu Senbin drove without a license, carried passengers in violation of regulations which impeded driving, and occupied the oncoming lane is based on clear facts and sufficient evidence, and should be confirmed. Accordingly, on December 19, 2000, the court entered judgment:

The part concerning the determination of liability in Document No. (2000) 343, "Decision on Re-determination of Road Traffic Accident Liability," made by the defendant Longyan Traffic Police Detachment, is revoked. Longyan Traffic Police Detachment shall, within 30 days from the effective date of this judgment, make a new liability determination for this accident.

Court acceptance fee of RMB 100 and other litigation costs of RMB 500 shall be borne by the defendant Longyan Traffic Police Detachment.

After the first instance judgment was pronounced, Longyan Traffic Police Detachment, dissatisfied, appealed. The grounds for appeal were: The appellee Li Zhifang's occupation of the oncoming lane is proven by the braking skid marks of the Jinbei minibus on the on-site investigation sketch and the road traffic accident photographs, and is an undeniable fact. The fact that the braking skid marks started 0.5 meters to the left of the road centerline only indicates that the vehicle began to leave braking skid marks from this point, and does not indicate that the vehicle had always been occupying only 0.5 meters to the left of the road before leaving the braking skid marks. In the circumstance of two vehicles meeting, Li Zhifang's occupation of the oncoming lane would inevitably affect the oncoming vehicle's ability to make a correct judgment. The original judgment's denial of the fact that Li Zhifang occupied the oncoming lane is a finding of unclear facts. We request that the first instance judgment be revoked and that the appellant's Document No. (2000) 343, "Decision on Re-determination of Road Traffic Accident Liability," be upheld.

The Longyan Intermediate People's Court of Fujian Province, upon second instance trial, found the facts to be the same as those found at first instance.

Opinion of Longyan Intermediate People's Court:

Article 17, paragraph 2 of the "Measures for the Handling of Road Traffic Accidents" (promulgated by State Council Decree No. 89 on September 22, 1991) provides: "If a party has a traffic violation, and the violation has a causal relationship with the traffic accident, the party shall bear liability for the traffic accident. If a party has no traffic violation, or although there is a traffic violation, the violation has no causal relationship with the traffic accident, the party shall not bear liability for the traffic accident." Article 19, paragraph 2 provides: "If the traffic violations of two parties jointly cause a traffic accident, the party whose violation played a greater role in the traffic accident shall bear primary liability, and the other party shall bear secondary liability; if the violations of the two parties played substantially equal roles in the traffic accident, the two parties shall bear equal liability."

In determining liability for a road traffic accident, it is first necessary to ascertain which conduct of each party at the time of the road traffic accident had a causal relationship with the occurrence of the accident, and then determine whether such conduct constituted a traffic violation and what liability the actor should bear. The on-site investigation sketch submitted by the appellant, Longyan Traffic Police Detachment, reflects that the effective width of the road at the accident section is 15.1 meters, with half-road width of 7.55 meters, and good line of sight on the road surface. The on-site investigation sketch and on-site photographs confirm that the collision point of the two vehicles was located in the lane driven by the appellee Li Zhifang's Jinbei minibus, at a point 0.46 meters from the road centerline. This is the position of the two vehicles at the time of the road traffic accident. Although the Jinbei minibus crossed the road centerline by 0.5 meters at the beginning of braking, there was still approximately 6 meters of effective road surface left on its left side. Even if Li Zhifang had not steered back into his own lane, the remaining effective road surface would have been sufficient for the oncoming two-wheel motorcycle driven by Qiu Senbin to pass safely. Furthermore, from the braking skid marks of the Jinbei minibus, the testimonies of witnesses Lin Qincai and Wu Qiang, and the interrogation record of Li Zhifang, it can also be seen that when the Jinbei minibus returned to its own lane, it was still more than 30 meters away from Qiu Senbin's motorcycle; from the time Li Zhifang detected the danger and took braking measures until the collision, Qiu Senbin's motorcycle was always in the position of occupying the oncoming lane. These circumstances all prove that although Li Zhifang had engaged in occupying the oncoming lane before detecting the danger, such conduct would not have caused Qiu Senbin, who was driving the oncoming motorcycle, to believe there was no way forward and thus take evasive measures by entering the opposite lane. Li Zhifang, upon detecting the danger, began braking and simultaneously steered back into his own lane. At that time, if Qiu Senbin, who was more than 30 meters away, had also steered into his own lane, the collision between the two vehicles could have been completely avoided. However, Qiu Senbin was driving without a license, and his lack of driving skill affected his ability to make a correct judgment; furthermore, due to the severe overloading of the motorcycle, Qiu Senbin was unable to maintain proper control of the vehicle's direction, causing him to fail to timely return to his own lane and instead collide with Li Zhifang's Jinbei minibus within Li Zhifang's lane. In this accident, Qiu Senbin's traffic violations, such as driving without a license, carrying passengers in violation of regulations, and occupying the oncoming lane, were clearly the main causes of the accident. However, Li Zhifang's traffic violation of occupying the oncoming lane had no causal relationship with the occurrence of the accident, and he should not be held liable for the accident based on this. Longyan Traffic Police Detachment's determination that Li Zhifang and Qiu Senbin each bear equal liability for this accident, on the ground that Li Zhifang occupied the oncoming lane, is clearly inappropriate. The first instance judgment, revoking the "Decision on Re-determination of Road Traffic Accident Liability" made by Longyan Traffic Police Detachment and ordering Longyan Traffic Police Detachment to make a new liability determination for this traffic accident, is correct. The appeal grounds of Longyan Traffic Police Detachment are untenable and should be dismissed. Accordingly, the Longyan Intermediate People's Court, in accordance with Article 61(1) of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC, on April 4, 2001, rendered judgment:

Appeal dismissed and the original judgment affirmed.

The court acceptance fee of RMB 100 for the second instance shall be borne by the appellant, Longyan Traffic Police Detachment.
